item.text: I’ll run the exact restore command, follow any refusal instructions to unstage `f` and resolve `c` with theirs, then report status and every command’s result. I won’t commit.

The command was refused with this message:

```text
git restore can overwrite uncommitted work. To unstage, run git reset -q -- <path> (always name the path: with none it resets the whole index); for a newly added file, git rm --cached -- <path> also works. To take a file's content from a conflict side or a commit, write it to a temporary file and, only if that succeeds, copy it over the file: tmp=$(mktemp) && git show "<src>" > "$tmp" && cp -- "$tmp" "<path>" && rm "$tmp", where <src> is :3:./<path> for theirs (:2:./<path> for ours; in a rebase :3: is your own commit being replayed) or <rev>:./<path> for a commit's version. Then run git add -- "<path>" as its own command. To take a side that deleted the file, run git rm --cached -- <path>, then rm -- <path>.
```

`c` now contains theirs and is staged. `f` remains on disk, unstaged and untracked. No commit was made.
